original.target_description: Experiment 3: interaction between velocity and stimulus width on reaction time to colour change; narrow (1.2°) versus wide (2.3°) sinusoidal-luminance segments, stationary or moving at 4.4 or 17.6°/s.

n.sample_role: Observers in Experiment 3, explicitly the same four as in Experiment 2; participant count, not the residual degrees of freedom or number of trials.
n.exclusions: Procedure almost identical to Experiment 1; Experiment 3 does not separately print final retained trial count or exclusion totals. No participant exclusion reported.
n.quote: Same four observers who participated in the previous ... experiment served as observers for this experiment, too.

es.location: Printed p. 1852 (PDF p. 5), §4.2, velocity × stimulus width interaction.
es.quote: between velocity and stimulus width [F (2, 4533) D 0.285; ... p < .753].

p.quote: between velocity and stimulus width [F (2, 4533) D 0.285; ... p < .753].

replication.target_description: The 2014 paper contains one unnumbered experiment with a fixed-size bar (1.2 × 2.3 degrees), not an Experiment 3 varying stimulus width. No velocity-by-width test located; the velocity-by-switch-point interaction is a different test and was not substituted.

notes:
Known replication target mismatch: no Experiment 3 or stimulus-width manipulation in the full paper. Its overall behavioral replication verdict cannot establish success for the assigned velocity-by-width interaction. Null statistics and analytic n because this target test is absent. Original full text unavailable after publisher 403 and repository timeout.
Source follow-up: Published article, Vision Research 46 (2006), pp. 1848–1855; supplied title/authors/DOI match. PDF page 5 rendered and inspected; no separately paginated embedded appendix. Canonical text D corresponds to equals sign in rendered PDF; F=0.285 and p < .753 confirmed visually. Less-than bound retained exactly as printed despite nonsignificant narrative. Ellipses omit interleaved text/column layout; original glyphs retained. No replication verdict extracted for original-only target.
